Soojin — thanks for flagging. High-level on Legal side after a quick read of the redline:
- Indemnity: Acme introduced a carve-out for subs in Section 7.3. We should push to keep Redwood's existing indemnity exposure capped at subcontractor proportionate liability (i.e., mirror current MSA language).
- Subcontractor approvals: MSA allows notice-only for 'non-core' subs; however, if any sub handles customer data (PII), we need explicit written approval + a DPA flow-down. The attached subcontractor sheet marks three companies that will process tokenized logs — need confirmation of their roles.
- DPA: The DPA_draft_acme_redwood.docx needs a clause tying subprocessor flow-downs and breach notification timelines to our standard 72-hour SLA. They did not include that.

Action items for us: (1) Request Acme to confirm which subs will have access to customer data; (2) propose a redline stating Redwood must receive written notice and can object within 10 business days; (3) include 72-hour breach notification and ability to require subprocessors to enter into a DPA equivalent to Redwood's DPA.

I'll draft suggested language this afternoon. cc: Marissa for procurement overlap.

— Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks for reviewing. Quick clarifications: the three subs marked in the sheet (DataStream Analytics, EdgeOps Ltd., and TokenLogix) will only collect tokenized telemetry for monitoring and are not intended to receive raw customer PII. We can provide architecture diagrams and a short SOC-lite report for each.

Acme's preferred timeline: we need approvals for those three by May 7 to hit internal supplier onboarding. If Redwood requires executed DPAs with each subprocessor, that will extend timelines — can you confirm whether a flow-down clause in the MSA plus an executed DPA between Redwood and Acme (with flow-down to subs) is acceptable so Acme doesn't have to sign three separate DPAs?

Best,
